methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $52M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Kinova Robotics is a late-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Charles Deguire and Louis-Joseph L'Ecuyer. The company has raised $51.6M to date. The comparable universe includes one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private peers in robotics and manufacturing, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity.

The analysis applies a stage-progression valuation method, which is the only applicable triangulation approach given data constraints. Using total capital raised of $52M as a proxy baseline, a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of late-stage to next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $62M. A peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the robotics sector; while eight peers exist in the broader sector, none met the screening criteria of three or more narrow-filtered datapoints.

The triangulated range is $53M (low) to $71M (high), with a median point of $62M. This single-method result carries meaningful uncertainty. The analysis lacks direct peer trading or funding multiples from sufficiently similar-stage companies, which limits precision. Key unknowns include Kinova's revenue scale, unit economics, and customer concentration relative to the identified peer set. Any valuation within this range should be stress-tested against proprietary financial performance and market position data.
